evals.prompt: /route-llm I'm building a coding agent that reads files, writes new functions, fixes bugs from test output, explains methods, and searches documentation
evals.expected_output: Produces a routing table with at least 3 task rows. Tier 1 for documentation search/explanation, Tier 2 for code writing and bug fixing, potentially Tier 3 for complex architecture tasks. Flags session pinning as required because tasks run in a multi-turn agent loop. Calculates a blended cost that is meaningfully lower than single-model opus pricing. Explains that switching models mid-loop would destroy prefix cache hits.

assertions.name: multi-tier-table
assertions.text: The routing table contains tasks assigned to at least 2 different tiers

assertions.name: session-pinning-required
assertions.text: Session pinning is flagged as required with explanation that model switching destroys prefix cache

assertions.name: cost-estimate
assertions.text: A blended cost estimate is provided showing reduction vs single frontier model

assertions.name: output-format
assertions.text: Response contains all required sections: Task Classification, Routing Table, Session Pinning, Cost Estimate, Implementation Notes

evals.prompt: /route-llm A customer support bot that classifies intent (billing, shipping, returns), extracts order numbers from messages, and responds with templated answers
evals.expected_output: All tasks classified as Tier 1 (haiku): intent classification, entity extraction, and template-fill are all cheap-model tasks. Session pinning is not required because this is a single-turn or stateless interaction pattern. Cost estimate shows very high reduction (80-90%) vs frontier model. No complex reasoning required.

assertions.name: tier-1-dominant
assertions.text: Most or all tasks are classified as Tier 1 (haiku-appropriate)

assertions.name: no-session-pinning
assertions.text: Session pinning is flagged as not required

assertions.name: high-cost-reduction
assertions.text: Cost estimate shows significant reduction (50%+) vs routing everything to frontier model

assertions.name: output-format
assertions.text: Response contains all required sections: Task Classification, Routing Table, Session Pinning, Cost Estimate, Implementation Notes

evals.prompt: /route-llm A document processing pipeline: OCR error correction on scanned text, extract named entities and dates, summarize each document, then produce a final investment recommendation weighing regulatory risk, market position, and financial metrics
evals.expected_output: Mixed tiers: OCR correction (Tier 1-2), entity extraction (Tier 1), summarization (Tier 1-2), final investment recommendation with multi-constraint reasoning (Tier 3). Session pinning not required because this is a batch pipeline, not an agent loop. Blended rate is mid-range. Tier 3 is reserved only for the final recommendation step.

assertions.name: tier-3-final-step
assertions.text: The final recommendation/reasoning step is classified as Tier 3

assertions.name: extraction-tier-1
assertions.text: Entity extraction or summarization tasks are classified as Tier 1 or Tier 2

assertions.name: no-session-pinning-batch
assertions.text: Session pinning is flagged as not required because this is a batch pipeline, not an iterative agent loop

assertions.name: output-format
assertions.text: Response contains all required sections: Task Classification, Routing Table, Session Pinning, Cost Estimate, Implementation Notes

evals.expected_output: Runs activate.sh to register the hook in .claude/settings.json and create the flag file ~/.claude/.route-llm-active. Confirms routing mode is active. Explains that each response will start with [ROUTING: Tier N — task — model]. Provides deactivation instructions. Mentions Claude Code restart may be needed for hook to take effect.

assertions.name: activate-script-run

assertions.name: routing-header-explained

assertions.name: deactivation-instructions
